# Mihari

> Mihari is an open-source identity, permissions and audit layer for AI agents. Each agent gets its own key and a signed identity card. Every tool call is checked against a policy (allow, ask a human, or deny), spend and rate limits apply, and each decision is written to a hash-linked audit log that can be verified offline. Free and self-hosted. Know your agent.

## Integrate

- MCP firewall: `MIHARI_AGENT_KEY=mia_… node packages/mcp/bin/mihari-mcp.js -- <your MCP server command>` (packages are not on npm yet; install the SDK with `npm install ./packages/sdk`). Blocked calls never reach the server; tools/list is trimmed to what the agent may use.
- Node SDK: `import {createMihari} from '@mihari/sdk'`; `guard.run({action, resource, amount}, tool)` fails closed.
- REST: `POST /api/authorize` with `Authorization: Bearer mia_…` and `{action, resource, amount, note}`. Response `decision.outcome` is `allow`, `ask` or `deny`. For `ask`, poll `GET /api/authorize/:eventId` until `status` is not `pending`. Then `POST /api/receipt`.
- Prove identity to a third party: `POST /api/assertion` `{audience}` returns a short-lived Ed25519 JWT. Verify offline with the registry public key from `GET /api/registry`, then check `GET /api/agents/:id/status` for revocation.

## On-chain identity (ERC-8004)

Each agent has an ERC-8004 registration file: `GET /api/agents/:id/registration.json`. The owner can publish it to the Identity Registry (Base Sepolia/Ethereum Sepolia `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e`, Base `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432`) with `register(string agentURI)`; the file travels as a `data:` URI. `GET /api/agents/:id/erc8004` (owner) returns the file and agentURI. `POST /api/agents/:id/onchain` `{chainId, agentId}` verifies ownership on-chain and links it. Assertions then include an `erc8004` claim. `GET /api/chain/lookup?chainId=&agentId=` reads any ERC-8004 agent.

## Policy model

Rules are `{action, resources[], mode: allow|ask|deny, maxAmount}`. `*` or a trailing `*` matches a prefix. Deny rules win; otherwise the first allow/ask rule that matches; no match means deny. Per-agent limits: `budget {amount, windowHours}`, `rate {count, windowMinutes}`, and credential expiry.

## Limits

Mihari decides and records; it cannot stop a tool call that bypasses the check. Outcome receipts are agent-reported. The audit log is tamper-evident relative to a known head, not a distributed ledger.

## Docs

/docs (quickstart, policy reference, API, MCP, assertions, security model), /verify (public assertion verifier).
